title: Voice (sustained sung vowels)
reference_instrument: adult male voice, sustained vowels (VocalSet long tones, CC BY 4.0)
summary: A lumped two-mass vocal-fold model phonates into a 44-section MRI-derived vocal tract and the radiated pressure is read at a baffled microphone. The oscillation is not imposed: it emerges from the fold, Bernoulli aperture, fold collision and tract loop. The tract comes from one male speaker's MRI area functions in a speech posture (Story 2008). These are exploratory fixtures, graded against VocalSet singers on the three notes they sang (C3, C4 and F4), one pair per vowel and note. Pitch, partial positions and inharmonicity are inside the real singers' spread on every graded pair, but pitch is matched by construction, so that is not evidence. The time-frequency picture, the spectral envelope, the attack time and the amount of natural fluctuation (the render is steadier than a sung vowel) are outside the real spread on most pairs. The pair files carry the measured numbers.
physics_present: Two-mass fold (Ishizaka-Flanagan masses and stiffnesses from the licensed model-card pack) as a port-Hamiltonian system with a Bernoulli aperture and fold collision, self-oscillating against the tract (fs-couple glottis.rs, fs-phs, fs-dcontact).

Vocal tract as a 44-section area function from Story (2008) Table I, with viscothermal loss and a flanged-piston radiation load from the transfer-matrix duct (fs-duct), played through a convergence-laddered characteristic line.

Mouth volume flow from the SAME transfer-matrix duct (driving_point::outlet, a laddered FIR driven by the island's incident wave), radiated through the baffled circular-opening receiver at the paper's recording geometry: 0.30 m, 45 degrees off axis.
Output is the retarded derivative of the physical mouth flow at the microphone; the supraglottal pressure is never the output and no source waveform, formant filter or gain is applied.

Every render's provenance sidecar reports the passive closed-glottis formants of its own tract, mouth load and wall (passive_tract_formants_hz). The native transfer-matrix result agrees with Story's own calculation to a few percent (/a/ F1/F2 669 / 956 Hz against his 694 / 942 Hz; his measured speaker has 715 / 1180 Hz), so the rendered tract is the published area function, not an artifact of the solver.
physics_missing: Tract wall: the rigid-wall descriptions leave the first formant with a bandwidth far below the 50 to 90 Hz measured for humans. The -flanagan descriptions add the published yielding-wall setting of Flanagan et al. (B 1.6e4 Pa s/m, M 15 kg/m^2, via Birkholz, Haesner and Kuerbis, ICASSP 2022) for C3, C4 and F4 /a/ and /o/; /e/, /i/ and /u/ at F4 are not provided. The wall stiffness is UNKNOWN in that source (its authors neglect it; 1.48e6 Pa/m is assumed and a six-fold change moves nothing). The wall is a uniform lumped pin, not a measured distribution along the tract, and Story's own calculation, which included walls, puts F1 of /i/ and /u/ 64 and 72 Hz above our rigid-wall passive F1.

Convergence ladders: the bead needs at least three rungs on every declared axis. The mechanics clock (the fold's time step) now has one: for /a/ at C4 with an ideal-open mouth the harmonics-to-noise ratio of the render rises from the 48 kHz clock through 96 and 144 kHz to 192 kHz and is converged there (384 kHz agrees), reaching the level of the real singers; with the real flanged mouth and the wall it rose from 96 to 192 kHz in all nine cases measured. The -flanagan-r4 descriptions use the 192 kHz clock and are the converged ones; the 96 kHz descriptions are under-resolved and leave a stationary non-harmonic floor that the singers do not have. Nothing else is laddered: the receiver's quadrature resolution, the tract line's tolerance and the fold's contact law.
Singing posture: the area functions are the speech configuration of the MRI subject, lying supine. Larynx height, pharynx and lip shape differ in singing, and no sung-posture MRI is entered.
Radiation: an infinite baffle replaces the head and torso, so there is no head diffraction. Nasal coupling, the piriform sinuses and other side cavities are not in the series plane-wave tract.

Fold tissue: a lumped two-mass card, not layered body-cover tissue or a 3D fold. The damping ratio and the collision law are authored estimates. Pitch is set by one stiffness factor per description, found by iterating the emergent f0 of the model alone to the target note (within 3 cents, no recording involved), so f0 matches by construction and is not evidence of fidelity. The factor differs between vowels at the same note (0.63 to 0.75 of the pack values at D#3) because the tract loads the fold; a physical fold-elongation law would replace this one free scale.

Subglottal system and player: the subglottal pressure is an authored player input (900 Pa times the stiffness factor), not a measured one, and there is no lung or trachea coupling. Vibrato, register changes and formant-tuning gestures are absent.

Regimes: the two-mass fold pair does not hold the target regime everywhere. At F4 the /a/, /e/ and /i/ pairs flip to a period-doubled oscillation (half the target frequency) within about 1% of the stiffness that gives the target, /i/ and /u/ found no usable F4 inside a sane stiffness range (/u/ only near 19 times the pack values), and /u/ at C4 oscillates irregularly (a broad comb of spectral lines, f0 spread 10.6 cents over four windows). F4 /a/ (+5.3 c) and /e/ (+9.6 c) are inside the bead's 10 cents but outside the 3 cents used elsewhere. C3, C4 and F4 exist because VocalSet's singers sang those notes.

Result of the wall on the largest graded gap, graded by P2 on the same slots: /u/ at C4 had an irregular oscillation (harmonics-to-noise far below every singer). Native probes showed it is not numerical (irregular at 48, 96 and 192 kHz mechanics clocks and for plus or minus one percent in stiffness; a rigid 96 kHz render stays irregular) and absent at C3 where f0 is far below the first formant. Adding the cited wall makes it regular and brings its harmonics-to-noise ratio and inharmonicity inside the singers' spread. Across all graded slots the wall is NOT a gain: the number of measures inside the real spread fell slightly. /u/ at C4 and /a/ at C4 moved outside on some other measures (the regular render sits further from the singers in spectrum and level pattern; the irregular one had matched some by accident), and several other one- or two-measure flips are at the edge of a wide ruler. The time-frequency picture and the spectral flux stay outside the real spread on most slots.

Natural fluctuation and onset: the subglottal pressure and fold tension are constant, so the render has no vibrato, tremor, jitter or shimmer from the player, and its phonation onset follows one fixed pressure ramp. The graded spectral flux and attack time differ from singers for that reason or a related one; the cause is not established. Cited measurements of player fluctuation would be needed as data.

/a/ at the converged clock: the flanged mouth load refused /a/ at 192 kHz (its mouth reaches ka 20.005 at that Nyquist against a bound of 20). The bound was a limit of the load's fixed quadrature design, not of the model it implements. Measured natively against the closed-form piston, the quadrature is accurate to 6.5e-14 across ka 20 to 26 and 2.9e-13 at 28, and loses its own 1e-12 gate at ka 30 (2.0e-11, then 3.6e-8 at 34 and 1.5e-5 at 38). The bound is now 24, tested at the cap and one unit above it. The /a/ descriptions at 192 kHz are not yet rendered or graded, so /a/ at C3, C4 and F4 is still described at the under-resolved 96 kHz clock, and the largest remaining graded harmonics-to-noise gap (/a/ at C4) is NOT cured until they are. A 384 kHz clock for /a/ (ka 40) stays refused: the quadrature does not resolve it.
